newsitem.title: USA: Brazil bond raised $1.5 bln of reserves -- Franco.
newsitem.headline: Brazil bond raised $1.5 bln of reserves -- Franco.

text.p: Brazil's $3.0 billion global bond deal added $1.5 billion to the country's international reserves, Brazilian central bank director of international affairs Gustavo Franco said Wednesday.
Brazil on Wednesday exchanged $3.0 billion of uncollateralized 30-year bonds for $1.622 billion of discount bonds, $542 million of par bonds, $86 million of C bonds and $750 million of cash.
Earlier Wednesday, the Brazilian central bank issued a statement that the country would recover about $605 million of U.S. Treasuries that was used as collateral for the par and discount bonds.
The freed collateral, coupled with the $750 million in cash garnered by the direct sale of the global bond, would be used to retire some of Brazil's internal debt, Franco told reporters here.
"The cash will be used immediately for retiring internal debt," Franco said, adding that the central bank needed to consider how it would handle the U.S. Treasury collateral.
"We have no intention of doing anything in a hurry," Franco said of the collateral. "We are in no hurry to sell."
Franco also said that the bond swap, in which Brazil reduced the principal amount of its debt by increasing the yield, would save the country $150-$200 million over the lifetime of the bonds.
"It has all the elements of a successful deal," Franco said, pointing to the overwhelming interest in the issue and how the spread tightened more than 20 points.
"We became more friendly to big institutional savers as we restructured away from rescheduled debt," he said. "What this deal shows is that there is a difference between Bradies and globals."
